target_customer: Women in India with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS), paying a subscription or buying supplements
problem: PCOS patients spend years and large sums finding treatment and most are dissatisfied with existing options.
business_model: Subscription app combining therapy, coaching and specialist support; later direct-to-consumer supplements
product_category: Women's health, digital therapeutics and nutraceuticals

founders.name: Shobhita Narain
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page; the company was started after she was diagnosed with PCOS.

technical_complexity.rationale: A subscription app with coaching and clinician workflow is standard consumer health engineering; the hard part is clinical evidence and operations, not software.

defensibility.rationale: Care protocols and a clinician network can be copied; published clinical research and customer outcomes offered limited protection.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; the company expanded into supplements under a Veera Wellness line.

market_need_then: The YC page cites 110M women in India with PCOS, years of diagnostic delay and widespread dissatisfaction with treatment; the July 2021 round was covered by several Indian outlets.

branding.brand_signature: Clinical credibility positioning, published research in ASRM, and Veera Wellness supplements

rebrands.to: Veera Health plus Veera Wellness supplements line
rebrands.why: Expansion into nutraceuticals to complement PCOS treatment; date from an Outlook India article of uncertain date

branding.community_and_virality: Site cites an 'As Seen In' press section and customer testimonials; no organic community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Regional consumer brand with press coverage and a product line, but no evidence of a mascot, community or viral pull.

pivots.to: Added direct-to-consumer supplements (VeeVital, Veera Wellness) and now a supplement-led storefront
pivots.why: To complement PCOS treatment; the date is unconfirmed

outcome_analysis: Veera Health raised a $3M seed in July 2021 and is active, but its public site has shifted from a PCOS treatment app toward supplements for weight loss, skin and PCOS. No later round was found; the shift suggests the original subscription model was not enough alone, though that is inference. Outcome is unresolved.
notes: No dated competitor source was found, so the list is empty (Gytree appears only in a 2025 article). Funding coverage is partial: only the 2021 round found. The Outlook India article date is unconfirmed. The pivot to supplements is inferred from the company site and the Outlook headline.
